svg.title: Figure 5. From a course report to affected versions: two cases
svg.desc: Two side-by-side panels showing the same configuration tree (U above H and S; H1, H2 under H; S1 under S). Left, change proposal CP-0001: a report received in H1 is traced to a shared cause in H (rule H-R03 lacks an exit condition), so H1 and H2 are the affected versions while S1 and the U-only baseline pass the scope check. Right, CP-0002: a report in H1 is traced to a local cause in H1 (an unavailable reading), so only H1 is affected and no shared change is proposed. Synthetic tests locate cause and scope before any correction is proposed.
svg.text: From a course report to affected versions: two cases
Where a weakness is discovered, where it is caused, and which versions share the cause are three different questions.
Report in H1: “it kept asking me the same question even after I said I didn't get it.”
Cause located in H: rule H-R03 has no exit condition when confusion persists.
Report in H1: the assistant “made up what chapter 4 said.” H1 references Hargreaves,
Reading the Archive, ch. 4, which is not in approved materials. H2 does not reference it.
Synthetic tests on U-only, H1, H2, S1 locate the cause and its scope; the dry runs confirmed CP-0001's pattern.
Reference design; identifiers are illustrative (fictional Wrenfield University).
